blocks.text: The chapter frames Rehoboam’s crisis as a pattern: abandoning the LORD is followed by prophetic warning, while humility is met with limited deliverance rather than complete destruction. The final assessment—that Rehoboam did evil because he did not set his heart to seek the LORD—connects the invasion and his response to the chapter’s larger concern with whether Judah seeks the LORD.

sections.title: A Pattern of Abandonment and Humility
